Parties camp here to take a long route in a single push rather than commit to a headlamp descent. Ground is a mix of heather bench and talus and the pads are small, so a large party will be split up. value.water: A snow-fed stream runs through the basin and usually carries water through the climbing season, but it thins as the snow patches under the peak melt out, which is why State Creek, low on the approach, is the last water to count on. Fill there, and carry enough for a dry night late in a hot summer.
value.permit: None. Dispersed camping on national forest land needs no permit, no reservation and no quota — the opposite of the North Cascades park zones a few miles west.
value.capacity: Several scattered one- and two-tent pads in the meadows and among the boulders; no established camp, so parties spread out
